content.title: About
content.content: Sausage NFS is a ready‑to‑eat meat product made from a blend of beef, pork and spices. The product is thermally processed and vacuum‑packed, providing a long shelf life without added preservatives.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: NFS stands for “No Further Seasoning”, meaning the product is ready to eat without additional seasoning.
The sausage is produced using a traditional recipe combined with modern vacuum‑packaging technology.
It is popular among hikers and for outdoor events because of its convenient transportability.
Only natural ingredients are used, with no artificial colourings.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: The sausage provides high‑quality animal protein essential for tissue repair.

items.title: Rich in iron
items.content: Meat products are a good source of heme iron, supporting normal blood formation.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamins B12, B6 and niacin, which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: Provides a quick source of calories, useful during periods of high physical activity.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to the product’s ingredients.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: The sausage contains a notable amount of salt; people with hypertension should limit intake.

items.title: Preservatives and nitrites
items.content: Certain batches may contain nitrite additives, which should be consumed in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sausage can be eaten straight from the pack, sliced for sandwiches, added to salads, or briefly pan‑fried. When heating, use moderate heat to avoid drying out the product.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator at 0 °C to +4 °C. Once opened, consume within 3–5 days. For longer storage, it can be frozen at –18 °C.
